column1: # Table 6 (Appendix E, "Positions which allow for line adjustment by interletter
# space-addition"), read from the English rendering, table_en7.pdf.
# Reconciliation note (ADR 0009): two independent hand transcriptions of this table were
# produced first (one per locale, without either seeing the other's work) and disagreed on
# a large number of cells -- overwhelmingly because Table 6's priority is encoded as a cell
# background color (E.1 id652-657) that a human transcriber cannot reliably distinguish by
# eye at PDF scale, exactly the failure mode ADR 0009 predicts for a from-image reading.
# Both hand transcriptions were therefore set aside as a *first pass* and this file (and its
# table6.ja.tsv pair) were built by mechanically extracting each PDF's own text layer and
# each cell's fill rectangle's non-stroking color (pdfplumber over table_en7.pdf and
# table_ja7.pdf independently, one extraction per document), then reading the fill color
# against the three colors the CMYK values decode to: (0.3,0,0,0) = cyan = id656 "1/4"
# (solid by default, expandable to a quarter-em ceiling), (0,0.3,0,0) = pink/magenta =
# id655 "1/4-1/2" (quarter-em by default, expandable to a half-em ceiling), (0,0,0,0.1) =
# gray = id657 (equal-share expansion with no stated ceiling, used only once every other
# expandable space is exhausted -- Sec 3.8.4 step (d), "residual" in this token vocabulary).
# The priority stage suffixes (`stage 2`, `stage 3`) are this reading's own addition, not
# printed in either PDF: Sec 3.8.4 states in words that the four steps of the expansion
# order are (a) the Western word space alone, up to a half em -- outside this pairwise
# matrix entirely, which is exactly why cl-26's row and column carry no colored cell of
# their own; (b) the quarter-to-half-em Japanese/Latin-boundary case, matching pink exactly
# by its own printed amount; (c) the general quarter-em-ceiling case "for places which do
# not fall under (a) or (b)", matching cyan's id656 wording exactly; and (d) the ordering
# residual, matching gray's id657 wording ("only after no other expandable inter-character
# spacing is left") word for word. Every note-anchored cell corroborates its color's stage:
# E.2 notes 4, 5, 6, 7, 10 and 12 each say "third order opportunity" of their cyan cell, and
# note 11 -- on a *white* cell -- offers "an alternative way to give a fourth order
# opportunity" only as a deviation from the table's own default reading of "blank".
# One cell disagreed between the two PDFs after this extraction, not merely between the two
# hand transcriptions: at cl-22, cl-22 the English rendering prints "n.6" and the Japanese
# rendering prints "注10）" (note 10), on cells that are otherwise identical (same cyan
# fill, same position). Note 6's text is about "different simple-ruby character complexes
# (cl-22)" -- this cell, exactly -- and note 10's text is about a preceding Western
# character (cl-27) before a trailing postfixed abbreviation (cl-13), a different pair
# entirely, already correctly and uniquely anchored at cl-27, cl-13 in *both* renderings.
# The Japanese PDF's "注10）" at cl-22, cl-22 is therefore read as a defect of that published
# document -- a duplicated/misprinted footnote number, the same species of defect
# docs/design/generation.md's "Recorded defects" section already catalogues twelve of for
# the HTML snapshot -- and not a genuine second reading to preserve. Both table6.en.tsv and
# table6.ja.tsv record `E.2#6` at this cell, which is what both PDFs' own cell content
# (color, position, and the note text itself) agree it means; only the Japanese PDF's
# printed footnote *glyph* disagrees, and that is recorded here in prose because
# spec/derived/defects.tsv is derived from the HTML snapshot only (docs/design/generation.md
# is explicit that none of its twelve rows is a property of a PDF matrix) and cannot carry a
# PDF-sourced defect without breaking `derive --check`'s byte-identity contract.
